A hard-edged shaft of warm sun drives down through a gap in the canopy and blazes on one magenta flower face while every surface around it stays blue-black and dripping.
The mist glows evenly as one enormous soft source so light arrives from every direction at once and the only shadows are the small dark pools pressed tight beneath each wet leaf.
Low late sun slides in sideways under the mist's belly and turns the soaked bark a deep bronze while the moss curtain hanging off it stays a flat, cold grey-green.
Rain-light flattens everything to silver and every beaded drop clinging to every leaf becomes a hard white point, the whole frame a field of tiny cold lights against near-black green.
Sun drives through one thin translucent fern leaf so the leaf itself reads as lit from inside, its veins bright gold-green, while the dark bark behind it stays near-black.
Light bounces upward off a rain-soaked limb and fills the shadow underneath a cluster of pale ivory flowers with a soft, reflected green glow.
A slot of brilliant white mist sits between two black trunks and every wet surface in front of it falls into deep blue-grey silhouette.
The last warm gold light climbs the upper trunk and stops there, leaving the scarlet flowers massed below it sitting in cold blue shade.
The mist thins for one moment and the wet leaves flare to an almost violent hot green before the white closes back in and swallows the colour.
A warm shaft from a break in the canopy picks out the standing water cupped in a ring of stiff leaves, making that one small pool the single brightest object in all the surrounding dark.
Blue-grey dusk fills the interior and one strip of white mist still lit far above reads as a pale bar between the black trunks, everything in front of it going slate-blue.
Storm-dark drops the whole frame to near-black but the violet flowers hold their own saturated colour hard against the blackened bark, refusing to go grey.
Dawn so cold the mist pressing between the trunks is blue-violet and the first thin sun striking the wet bark is a sharp warm orange line climbing from root to branch.

Heavy overcast turns every wet surface into a dark mirror, bark near-black and mirror-bright, and against all that near-black the one orchid holds its full scarlet as the only saturated thing in the frame.
A rim of warm amber light catches the very edge of a broad wet leaf, outlining it against the cold dark interior, so only that one curved rim glows and everything else falls away.

A thin shaft of sunlight drops straight through a single gap and strikes the beaded surface of a moss curtain, igniting hundreds of water drops to white-gold against the surrounding deep green shadow.
Reflected light bounces off standing water pooled in a hollow of bark and throws a rippled pale-blue pattern up onto the underside of the leaves directly above it.
A wide diffuse warm-orange glow seeps in from one low gap between trunks at one side, fading within centimetres into the cold blue-green shadow that owns the rest of the frame.
Midday and the mist sits thick, pressing the light flat and cold, but a single egg-yellow flower cluster catches what little there is and holds it, the one bright thing in all the grey-green dark.
A shaft of sun breaks through and strikes the wet surface of a broad leaf at a raking angle so the water film on it blazes white-silver and the leaf's own deep green reads below it.
Late in the day a wedge of warm copper light presses in between two trunks and lies right along the top of a near limb, turning its soaking moss to amber while the mist above it stays blue and unlit.
The mist brightens from within for a minute, going from grey to a cool luminous white, and the wet bark closest to it picks up that cold white on its raised ridges while the deep crevices stay black.

A gap between two trunks lets a hard bar of white mist-light fall across a single orchid face, bleaching its centre to near-white while its outer petals stay a deep, saturated blue-purple in the shade.

Soft green light reflected off a moss-covered limb wraps the underside of every flower and leaf above it in a faint cool-green fill, erasing the hard shadows and making the whole lower half of the frame glow faintly.

One crack in the canopy lets a pencil-thin beam of warm yellow light travel all the way down to a pool of standing water held in a hollow in the wet bark, splitting into a small bright star while the trunks on all sides stay black.
